rows.title: Graduate Analyst Programme - Public Sector Consulting
rows.descriptionText:
About Baringa

Baringa is a global consulting firm that partners with leaders to drive change and create value. With deep industry expertise, and enabled by advanced technology, the firm helps clients to deliver with greater confidence and certainty. With over 2,000 people across the UK, Europe, North America, Asia and Australia, the firm combines global insight with local understanding.

The firm works across energy and resources, financial services, government and public sector, consumer products and retail, pharmaceuticals and life sciences, manufacturing, and technology, media and telecoms, with capabilities spanning strategy, transformation and operational excellence – all powered by advanced technology, data, AI and digital innovation.

Clients value Baringa’s collaborative approach and the way its teams integrate seamlessly – all working with a shared understanding of what matters most. The firm is known for its kind, curious experts who listen closely and care deeply about client success as they help clients transform energy markets, modernise financial platforms, expand telecoms and digital networks through advanced data analytics, enable digital services in government, and unlock growth in consumer sectors.

Certified as a Great Place to Work around the world, Baringa has been recognised by the Financial Times in 22 categories of its UK Leading Management Consultants rankings, and by Forbes for four consecutive years as one of the World’s Best Management Consulting Firms.

Our Analyst Roles

Our Analyst roles give you the opportunity to build a career in an award-winning management consultancy firm while contributing to meaningful client work from day one. You will develop an understanding of the consulting business model as well as hands-on experience across the consulting project lifecycle, from understanding client challenges and analysing evidence through to developing recommendations and supporting delivery.

As an Analyst you will join a real consulting team, working and learning from experienced consultants, with exposure to meaningful client work alongside structured development to help you learn more about Baringa and working as a consultant.

About The Government Team At Baringa

Our Government team helps departments, agencies and public services solve complex problems and deliver better outcomes for citizens. Our work spans Central Government, Home Affairs, and Health and Public Infrastructure, from redesigning services and strengthening operations to using data, technology and AI to improve decisions and delivery.

We work on Government’s most complex changes, partnering with departments across Whitehall and the wider public sector, using our skills in Strategy and Business Cases, Project Delivery, Operational Delivery, DDaT and Government Commercial.

The UK public sector is navigating significant challenges and opportunities, including the delivery of major national priorities and missions. As our Public Sector team continues to grow, we are looking for curious and motivated Analysts who are excited to learn, contribute and develop with us. You do not need previous consulting or public sector experience – we are interested in how you approach problems, learn new things and apply your skills to real-world challenges.

What you will be doing

We will embed you in client projects as part of a consulting team, working alongside experienced consultants to learn while delivering real client outcomes. You will not be expected to know how to do all of this from day one. You will be supported throughout and given opportunities to build your skills through meaningful project work.

Depending on the project you join, you may have the opportunity to:

Analyse quantitative and qualitative information to identify insights, trends and opportunities for improvement.Explore how data, digital technology, automation or AI could help improve public services.Develop recommendations and delivery plans, considering how people, technology and data work together.Support the development of client materials, including presentations, reports, workshop outputs and project updates.Contribute to meetings and workshop discussions, helping to capture key points, actions and decisions.Learn how consulting teams work together to solve problems, structure ambiguous challenges and communicate clearly with clients and colleagues.

Examples of the type of projects you could be working on are:

Support transformation projects that help government and public sector organisations improve services, strengthen operations and deliver better outcomes for citizens.Help review how services and processes work, from frontline delivery through to internal operations, identifying opportunities to make them simpler, more effective or more resilient.Contribute to digital, data and analytics work, including projects that use AI or data-led approaches to help clients make better decisions.Support the development of business cases and funding proposals, helping clients assess different options and make evidence-based decisions.Help design how services should operate, looking at how people, processes, technology and data come together to deliver better results within operating models and service blueprints.Support commercial and procurement activity, such as researching suppliers, comparing options and helping prepare materials for decision-making.

What are we looking for?

We welcome applications from students across a broad range of academic disciplines, including STEM and non-STEM subjects, and are particularly keen to hear from students who enjoy solving complex problems using evidence, data, technology and creative thinking. You do not need to have previous experience in consulting or the public sector - what matters most is your curiosity, willingness to learn and interest in helping public sector organisations solve complex challenges.

Skills

We are looking for people who are excited by the opportunity to learn how consulting teams work, contribute to meaningful client projects and develop their skills in a supportive environment. You may be a good fit if you bring:

Structured problem solving, with the ability to break down unfamiliar questions and identify what matters.Data analysis skills, and comfort working with data to surface insight and support evidence-based recommendations. Digital and AI literacy, with genuine curiosity about AI and its practical application, and a foundational understanding of how to use these tools responsibly and ethically.Interest in policy, government and public service, and how national priorities translate into delivery on the ground.Commercial and financial curiosity, with an interest in how money, value and delivery decisions shape public services, and comfort working with numbers to support them.Clear communication skills, including the ability to explain ideas simply and structure your thinking in writing and conversation.A collaborative approach, with enthusiasm for working in teams and learning from others.Willingness to learn and adapt, particularly in a fast-paced project environment where priorities can evolve.Attention to detail and ownership, taking pride in the quality of your work and following through on tasks.A proactive attitude, with the confidence to ask questions, contribute ideas and get involved.

We do not expect you to have all the answers from day one. We are looking for potential, enthusiasm and a genuine interest in developing your consulting skills while contributing to work that matters.

What's in it for you?

An Analyst role at Baringa is what you make it.

This is a permanent role where you will gain real project experience alongside structured coaching, training and development. You will build your analytical, communication and problem-solving skills while learning how to support clients, work within high-performing teams and grow as a consultant.

You will be part of a collaborative, supportive environment where you can learn from experienced consultants, explore different types of public sector work, and build a long-term career with Baringa.

Requirements

Applicants should have a strong academic record or equivalent experience, with an interest in consulting and public sector work. Applicants must have the permanent right to work in the UK now and in the future and be eligible for a UK Security Check (SC) clearance. All applicants will be asked for proof if invited to an assessment centre.

Please note we’re unable to sponsor individuals for this opportunity.

Key dates

Application window closes: Monday 19th October, 12pm GMT Midday

Assessment centres: New Year 2027

We are looking for individuals to start with Baringa May & September 2027

What a career at Baringa will give you

Putting People First.

Benefits

Baringa is a People First company and wellbeing is at the forefront of our culture. We recognise the importance of work-life balance and flexible working and provide our staff amazing benefits. Some of these benefits include:

Generous Annual Leave Policy: We recognise everyone needs a well-deserved break. We provide our employees with 5 weeks of annual leave, fully available at the start of each year. In addition to this, we have introduced our 5-Year Recharge benefit which allows all employees an additional 2 weeks of paid leave after 5 years continuous service. Flexible Working: We know that the ‘ideal’ work-life balance will vary from person to person and change at different stages of our working lives. To accommodate this, we have implemented a hybrid working policy and introduced more flexibility around taking unpaid leave. Corporate Responsibility Days: Our world is important to us, so all our employees get 3 every year to help social and environmental causes and increase our impact on the communities that mean the most to us. Wellbeing Fund: We want to encourage all employees to take charge and prioritise their own wellbeing. We’ve introduced our annual People Fund to support this by offering every individual a fund to support and manage their wellbeing through an activity of their choice. Profit Share Scheme: All employees participate in the Baringa Group Profit Share Scheme so everyone has a stake in the company’s success. 

Diversity and Inclusion

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We believe that creating an environment where everyone feels a sense of belonging is central to our culture and that diversity is paramount to driving creativity, innovation, and value for our clients and for our people.

An award-winning workplace

You can be a part of our ‘Great Place to Work’ – with our commitment to women and well-being in the workplace for all. Click here to see some of our recent awards and how we’ve achieved this.

Using business as a force for good.

We maintain high standards of environmental performance and transparency, which can be seen through our commitment to Net Zero with our SBTI-verified Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions reduction targets and our support of the Better Business Act. We report our progress publicly and ensure that we are also externally assessed and scored through organisations like CDP and EcoVadis - helping us to continually identify where we can improve.

We have a long legacy of supporting the communities in which we work, and offer a variety of ways to contribute, by putting people first and creating impact that lasts. Our Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) agenda is about giving back to the communities in which we live and work by sharing our skills, talent and time. In essence, we aim to empower and encourage everyone in the firm to contribute to the things we care about, and support registered charities and organisations with a clear social or environmental purpose to increase the positive impact they can have.

Join us

All applications received will be reviewed by a member of our Talent Acquisition team. We never rely solely on automated screening or AI tools to make hiring decisions. Your application will be considered for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, nationality, disability, age, faith or social background. We do not filter applications by university background and encourage those who have taken alternative educational and career paths to apply. We would like to actively encourage applications from those who identify with less represented and minority groups. We operate an inclusive recruitment process, ensuring reasonable adjustments where needed. Please contact a member of our Recruitment Team to discuss further.

Baringa Privacy Notices

For UK & EU

Your personal data will be retained by Baringa for up to two years, in accordance with our UK Recruitment Privacy Notice / EU Recruitment Privacy Notice, to evaluate your application and meet our legal and reporting obligations. In line with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), you have the right to request access to, rectification, or erasure (subject to legal limitations) of your personal data. For more information, please contact us at privacy@baringa.com

For the USA

Your personal data may be retained by Baringa for up to two years, as outlined in our Recruitment Privacy Notice (AMER & APAC), to support the recruitment process and internal reporting requirements. Where applicable, and in accordance with relevant federal and state laws, you may have the right to request access to or correction of your personal information. For further details, please contact privacy@baringa.com

For Australia & Singapore

Your personal data will be retained by Baringa for up to two years, in accordance with our Recruitment Privacy Notice (AMER & APAC), to assess your application and meet applicable reporting and legal obligations. In line with the Australian Privacy Act and Singapore’s Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA), you may have rights to access, correct, or request limited deletion of your personal data. For more information, please contact us at privacy@baringa.com

rows.title: Intelligence Analyst II
rows.descriptionText:
About Crisis24

Crisis24 is a global, AI-enhanced provider of travel risk management, mass communications, critical event management, crisis-security consulting, personal protection solutions and global medical concierge capabilities, allowing prominent organizations, disruptive brands and influential people to operate with confidence in an uncertain world. At Crisis24, we go beyond mere employment; we pave the way to a realm where your skills become instrumental in shaping global security, guiding clients through a multifaceted and challenging landscape. Your journey with us will be deeply fulfilling, driven by a powerful sense of purpose and accomplishment. Within our thriving environment, you'll discover abundant chances for both personal and career advancement. Seize this moment to push your limits, broaden your expertise, and elevate your professional journey to unprecedented levels. Join the Crisis24 team today and be a part of something extraordinary where growth and impact converge.

More information is available at www.crisis24.garda.com

Who We Are Looking For

We are seeking full-time GSOC Analysts to join an embedded Global Security Operations Centre (GSOC), providing 24/7/365 support to global operations. The GSOC supports the security function of a multinational client with a global footprint, requiring close collaboration with client stakeholders in a dynamic international environment. This role is suited for candidates with strong research and professional writing skills, and with previous experience in, or a strong interest in, global security, geopolitics, intelligence, and investigations. The role is primarily operational in nature, while also including investigative and analytical responsibilities to support security operations, incident response, and stakeholder reporting. The successful candidate will be a strong team player who can also work independently with minimal supervision, manage competing priorities, and deliver accurate work to tight deadlines. They should be comfortable working in a fast-paced operational environment and communicating clearly and professionally with a wide range of stakeholders. This is an office-based role located at the Crisis24 office in central London. As the GSOC provides continuous 24/7 coverage, the position requires regular office presence and operates on a shift-based rota, including night shifts, weekends, and public holidays. The ideal candidate will therefore be based in the London area or within a commutable distance of central London. Successful applicants typically have 1-4 years of experience.

Fluency in Arabic or Portuguese would be highly desirable.

What You Will Work On

Monitor global security developments through a range of sources, including internal reporting, stakeholders, open-source, social media, and intel monitoring platformsIdentify, assess, and escalate incidents requiring attention, and support relevant stakeholders in their responsePrepare and distribute security alerts, warnings, situational awareness updates, and travel security communicationsSupport emergency notification processes during incidents, crises, exercises, and other relevant situationsContact employees and travellers during emergencies and provide timely updates to key stakeholders, as requiredCoordinate with regional and global security teams in response to significant incidents requiring cross-regional supportSupport crisis management activities, exercises, and event security operationsProvide security and crisis management support to employees and business travellersAct as a point of contact for employees and travellers by managing security communication channels and responding to security-related queries and requests for supportSupport travel security processes, including the monitoring of submissions, approvals, and traveller tracking where requiredProvide pre-travel security advice and support to travellersCoordinate actions in line with crisis management procedures, evacuation plans, and other security protocolsSupport the maintenance of accurate records relating to sites, employees and travellers, ensuring information can be made available quickly during incidents, crises, or exercisesMonitor access control and CCTV systems, where requiredCarry out any other GSOC-related duties as directed by the GSOC Manager, Regional Security Directors, or key stakeholders

Who You Will Work With

The Security Analyst will be part of the Global Security Operations Centre (GSOC) team, supporting the delivery of operational security monitoring, incident response, crisis management, and traveller support. The role will work closely with the GSOC Manager, Regional Security Directors, and other members of the client’s Security function, as well as employees and key stakeholders across the organisation.

What You Will Bring

1–4 years of relevant experience in security operations, intelligence, investigations, or a related fieldStrong research, analytical, and professional writing skills, with the ability to deliver clear, accurate, and timely output in a fast-paced environmentExcellent written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to communicate complex issues clearly and professionally to a range of stakeholdersPrevious experience in, or a strong interest in, global security, geopolitics, intelligence, or investigationsThe ability to assess information, exercise sound judgement, and escalate issues appropriately in support of security operations and incident responseA sound understanding of security-related issues in a corporate or operational environment, and the ability to make balanced, business-relevant decisionsStrong organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities, meet deadlines, and perform effectively under pressureStrong interpersonal skills and a collaborative approach, with the ability to work both independently and as part of a teamConfidence in using a range of systems and technology to support operational monitoring, communication, and stakeholder engagementA bachelor’s degree, or equivalent experience, in a relevant discipline such as International Relations, Security Studies, Intelligence, Criminology, or a related fieldFluency in Arabic or Portuguese would be highly desirable

 PLACES PEOPLE PREFER 

Our purpose is to create and manage outstanding places which deliver positive outcomes for all our stakeholders on a long term, sustainable basis.

We are a FTSE listed business with a strong balance sheet and £15.2bn of assets under management. But with just 600 employees you’re given the ability to make a big impact and elevate your career quickly.

Our diverse, passionate team of experts works on some of the most ambitious, innovative and sustainable projects in the country – from our high-quality campuses across central London, to some of the top retail schemes in the UK – providing a rewarding career journey where you can shape how you grow.

We believe in shared success and enabling people to be themselves. If you want to feel listened to and understood in an environment where your opinions count and bright ideas are encouraged, you’ve come to the right place!

In our latest engagement survey, 81% of colleagues said they are proud to work at British Land!

 THE ROLE 

The Sustainability Analyst will play a key role in supporting the delivery and measurement of British Land's Social Sustainability Strategy and wider Sustainability ambitions.

This role combines programme coordination, data management and stakeholder engagement responsibilities. Day-to-day activities include coordinating defined social impact data collection,

maintaining reporting systems and supporting the validation and analysis of social value data across British Land's portfolio.

The analyst will work closely with internal teams, charity partners and external stakeholders to support effective programme delivery, governance processes and preparation of complete, accurate and timely reporting information.

The successful candidate will operate effectively within a matrix environment, balancing priorities across programme delivery and reporting requirements. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who is passionate about creating positive social impact and keen to develop expertise across community investment, social value, and sustainability reporting.

What You’ll Do

 Coordinate social impact data collection and undertake first-line validation across British Land's retail, campus and development portfolios.  Support reporting against British Land's social sustainability targets, annual sustainability reporting requirements and external benchmarks.  Maintain reporting systems, user records, process documentation and audit evidence.  Coordinate Social Impact Committee governance processes, including agendas, papers, action tracking and meeting records.  Track programme expenditure, commitments and budgets, escalating discrepancies to the appropriate budget owner.  Act as an operational point of contact for charity partners and community organisations.  Support the management of employee matched funding and payment processes.  Support delivery of social impact programmes across education, employment, volunteering and community investment priorities.  Act as a key user for Thrive, Optimy and other social impact systems, supporting user access, reporting and process improvements.  Identify opportunities to improve reporting quality and operational efficiency. 

About You

 Degree qualified in Sustainability, Social Sciences, Geography, Business, Community Development, Data Analysis or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience and a demonstrated interest in social impact.  Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.  Proficiency in Excel and Data Management Systems.  Experience collecting, validating and managing information from multiple sources.  Excellent organisational and time management skills.  Strong written and verbal communication skills.  Ability to build effective relationships across teams and with external stakeholders.  Ability to manage multiple priorities and workstreams simultaneously.  Organised, proactive and self-motivated with a continuous improvement mindset.  Passion for social impact, sustainability and community investment. 

Desired Knowledge And Experience

 Experience administering grant-making, community investment or social impact programmes.  Experience working with reporting systems, databases or CRM platforms.  Experience supporting reporting, assurance or audit processes.  Experience using Dashboards, Power BI or similar tools.  Understanding of social value measurement, community investment or sustainability reporting 

frameworks.

 Experience working with charities, community organisations or social enterprises. 

 OUR SHARED VALUES  our values are what we stand for at British Land, they’re not just a label on the door; they connect us every day to our vision, purpose, and strategy. They help us to promote an inclusive, positive, and collaborative culture. You can read more on our corporate website .

Bring your whole self

Listen & Understand

Smarter together

Build for the future

Deliver at pace

 A REWARDING PLACE TO BE 

Our People – Just ask anyone why they love working here and they will tell you it’s the people. They’re highly talented, passionate, and collaborative! We thank our people with rewards that feel rewarding; you can review our market leading benefits here .

 OUR RECRUITMENT PROCESS 

If you enjoy bringing your whole self to work, share our values and are excited about our purpose we’d love to hear from you! We are committed to providing an accessible and inclusive process learn more about our selection process here.

Please note that we endeavour to get back to all applicants within 28 days. If you haven’t heard from us within this period, please assume that you have been unsuccessful on this occasion.

rows.title: Graduate Analyst Programme - Capabilities
rows.descriptionText:
About Baringa

Baringa is a global consulting firm that partners with leaders to drive change and create value. With deep industry expertise, and enabled by advanced technology, the firm helps clients to deliver with greater confidence and certainty. With over 2,000 people across the UK, Europe, North America, Asia and Australia, the firm combines global insight with local understanding.

The firm works across energy and resources, financial services, government and public sector, consumer products and retail, pharmaceuticals and life sciences, manufacturing, and technology, media and telecoms, with capabilities spanning strategy, transformation and operational excellence – all powered by advanced technology, data, AI and digital innovation.

Clients value Baringa’s collaborative approach and the way its teams integrate seamlessly – all working with a shared understanding of what matters most. The firm is known for its kind, curious experts who listen closely and care deeply about client success as they help clients transform energy markets, modernise financial platforms, expand telecoms and digital networks through advanced data analytics, enable digital services in government, and unlock growth in consumer sectors.

Certified as a Great Place to Work around the world, Baringa has been recognised by the Financial Times in 22 categories of its UK Leading Management Consultants rankings, and by Forbes for four consecutive years as one of the World’s Best Management Consulting Firms.

Our Graduate Analyst Programme

Our Graduate Analyst role offers the opportunity to start and grow your career at Baringa. As a permanent member of our team from day one, you'll work on a variety of real client and internal projects, develop valuable skills, and make a meaningful contribution from the outset.

You'll work alongside experienced consultants, building both your technical and professional capabilities through structured learning, hands-on experience, and ongoing development opportunities. Along the way, you'll build relationships across the business, collaborate with colleagues from different teams and sectors, and contribute to work that makes a real impact.

If you're a recent graduate looking to kick-start your career, Baringa offers a supportive and collaborative environment where you can develop your skills, gain practical experience, and build a successful long-term future with us.

We're looking for Graduate Analysts to join our Capabilities practice, with opportunities available across several of our specialist business units. During the application process, you'll have the opportunity to select the business unit that best aligns with your interests and aspirations.

The Business Units Currently Hiring Are

Customer

Imagine a world where customers are delighted, employee engagement soars and costs drop. This is the power of world-class omni-channel experiences. Our expert team anticipates change, crafting innovative solutions that blend seamlessly across all touchpoints. By leveraging cutting-edge technology, we transform service delivery, minimising costs while maximising impact. Ready to enhance your market position and unlock unprecedented value? Let’s redefine excellence together.

Desired Skills: Strong communication, teamwork, and relationship-building skills. Structured problem-solving and analytical thinking. A customer-focused mindset and interest in improving customer experiences. AI and digital literacy with a curiosity for emerging technologies. Adaptability, curiosity, and a proactive approach to learning and development.

Desired Degrees: Business Management, Product Design UX & UI, and Marketing

Enterprise Value Creation

Every organisation faces moments when it needs to grow faster, operate more efficiently or respond to changing market conditions. Baringa's Enterprise Value Creation team helps clients navigate these challenges by combining strategic thinking, analytical rigour, AI-native mindset, and practical delivery expertise. We advise executive leadership teams to identify opportunities, solve complex business problems and deliver sustainable improvements in growth, profitability, and performance.

Desired Skills: Structured problem solving, Data analysis, Digital and AI literacy, Team collaboration and personal communication, Adaptability, Commercial and financial curiosity.

Desired Degrees: Open to all degree types.

Organisation, People & Change 

Organisation, People, and Change (OPC) enables organisations to achieve lasting success by putting people at the centre of transformation. With a holistic approach, our team helps clients align their operating models, people strategies, structures, and cultures with their strategic ambitions. OPC ensures organisations are equipped to deliver impact that lasts through an engaged and high-performing workforce.

As Part Of OPC, You Will Have The Opportunity To Work Across a Range Of Sectors, Helping Clients With a Range Of Solutions

Optimising operations and organisational design: Align business capabilities, processes, and technology with the strategic ambition to drive efficiency and effectiveness.Unlocking leadership, culture, and workforce potential: Shape future skills, foster an engaged and high-performing workforce, and embed target cultures through people-led experiences.Crafting and delivering transformation and change strategies: Define the vision, strategic direction, and OKRs to create positive conditions for change, enabling organisations to deliver lasting impact.

Desired Skills: Excellent communication and collaboration skills, Strong critical thinking and problem-solving abilities, Organisation and project management capability, Curiosity, adaptability, and a growth mindset, AI literacy and an interest in innovation, A genuine passion for consulting and transforming organisations and workforces through meaningful change.

Desired Degrees (not essential): Business management / Management and Organisational Behaviour, Psychology / Organisational Psychology, Engineering - critical thinking / problem solving, Data Analytics / Business Analytics.

Supply Chain & Procurement 

The SCP team helps organisations tackle complex challenges across their supply chains, procurement functions and commercial operations. Working with clients across the public and private sectors, we help organisations navigate an increasingly uncertain world, responding to challenges such as cost pressures, supply chain disruption, changing customer expectations and rapid technological change.

As part of SCP, you'll work on a diverse range of projects spanning supply chain strategy, procurement transformation, commercial advisory, logistics, and technology-enabled change, as part of either our Supply Chain or Procurement & Commercial practice. Our teams combine analytical thinking, practical problem-solving and deep industry expertise to help clients create efficient, resilient and sustainable organisations that deliver lasting value.

Desired Skills: Structured problem solving, Team collaboration and effective communication, Adaptability and personal resilience, Proactive curiosity, Digital literacy.

Desired Degrees: No degree preference, analytical capabilities are key. If you have commercial acumen this is a bonus. Candidates may benefit from STEM experience, but this is not a requirement.

Data, AI, Solutions & Engineering

Expertly applied, data and AI empower you to operate smarter, innovate faster and compete harder. Blending exceptional technical skills with deep industry knowledge, our consultants make the possibilities real. We are experts in crafting practical data and AI solutions and integrating these into existing production workflows. Where data and AI requires new scalable technology, we work with you to establish the case for investment. And when new data insights are revealed, we ensure you have the right talent to unlock full value. Whether you are looking to establish a robust data infrastructure, foster a data-driven culture or ensure data and information security and compliance are maintained, we can help.

Desired Skills: Problem Solving, Data Analysis, Data Literacy, Technical Data Skills - BI, Python, Engineering, ML, Other coding languages.

Desired Degrees: STEM, Computer Science, Data Science, Other technical data/AI degrees

So, what's in it for you?

You’ll join with a cohort of our Graduate Analysts. As a cohort, you will participate in our Analyst Development Programme. Our programme is designed to develop the client, commercial and people skills that you need for a successful career at Baringa. You will join our Global Analyst Community, connecting Analysts with one another to share their experiences and lessons learnt, whilst also gaining knowledge and skills from experienced Baringa people You decide on the development you need. We invest in you, to ensure you remain the best in the business, through formal training and qualifications, coaching and mentoring. You can talk to anyone in the business. There are no barriers, and everyone is accessible, from our Analysts to our Partners. Out Partner to consultant ratio of 1:10, means you get to learn and work alongside our Directors and Partners on a daily basis. We’re proud to put people first with wellbeing at the forefront of our culture, one example of this is that every employee receives £300 a year to put towards their wellbeing!All employees participate in the Baringa Group Profit Share Scheme, which seeks to ensure that everyone has a stake in the success of the company. We recognise everyone needs a well-deserved break - As such we have introduced the ‘Re-charge’ benefit meaning Baringa will offer all employees an additional 2 weeks of paid leave after 5 years continuous service. Lastly, we recognise the importance of work-life balance and we know that the ‘ideal’ balance will vary from person to person and will change at different stages of our working lives. 

Requirements

Applicants must have the permanent right to work in the UK now and in the future.All applicants will be asked for proof if invited to an assessment centre.

Please note we’re unable to sponsor individuals for this opportunity.

Key dates

Application window closes: Monday 19th October, 12pm GMT Midday

Assessment centres: New Year 2027

We are looking for individuals to start with Baringa September 2027

What a career at Baringa will give you

Putting People First.

Benefits

Baringa is a People First company and wellbeing is at the forefront of our culture. We recognise the importance of work-life balance and flexible working and provide our staff amazing benefits. Some of these benefits include:

Generous Annual Leave Policy: We recognise everyone needs a well-deserved break. We provide our employees with 5 weeks of annual leave, fully available at the start of each year. In addition to this, we have introduced our 5-Year Recharge benefit which allows all employees an additional 2 weeks of paid leave after 5 years continuous service. Flexible Working: We know that the ‘ideal’ work-life balance will vary from person to person and change at different stages of our working lives. To accommodate this, we have implemented a hybrid working policy and introduced more flexibility around taking unpaid leave. Corporate Responsibility Days: Our world is important to us, so all our employees get 3 every year to help social and environmental causes and increase our impact on the communities that mean the most to us. Wellbeing Fund: We want to encourage all employees to take charge and prioritise their own wellbeing. We’ve introduced our annual People Fund to support this by offering every individual a fund to support and manage their wellbeing through an activity of their choice. Profit Share Scheme: All employees participate in the Baringa Group Profit Share Scheme so everyone has a stake in the company’s success. 

Diversity and Inclusion

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We believe that creating an environment where everyone feels a sense of belonging is central to our culture and that diversity is paramount to driving creativity, innovation, and value for our clients and for our people.

An award-winning workplace

You can be a part of our ‘Great Place to Work’ – with our commitment to women and well-being in the workplace for all. Click here to see some of our recent awards and how we’ve achieved this.

Using business as a force for good.

We maintain high standards of environmental performance and transparency, which can be seen through our commitment to Net Zero with our SBTI-verified Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions reduction targets and our support of the Better Business Act. We report our progress publicly and ensure that we are also externally assessed and scored through organisations like CDP and EcoVadis - helping us to continually identify where we can improve.

We have a long legacy of supporting the communities in which we work, and offer a variety of ways to contribute, by putting people first and creating impact that lasts. Our Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) agenda is about giving back to the communities in which we live and work by sharing our skills, talent and time. In essence, we aim to empower and encourage everyone in the firm to contribute to the things we care about, and support registered charities and organisations with a clear social or environmental purpose to increase the positive impact they can have.

Join us

All applications received will be reviewed by a member of our Talent Acquisition team. We never rely solely on automated screening or AI tools to make hiring decisions. Your application will be considered for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, nationality, disability, age, faith or social background. We do not filter applications by university background and encourage those who have taken alternative educational and career paths to apply. We would like to actively encourage applications from those who identify with less represented and minority groups. We operate an inclusive recruitment process, ensuring reasonable adjustments where needed. Please contact a member of our Recruitment Team to discuss further.

Baringa Privacy Notices

For UK & EU

Your personal data will be retained by Baringa for up to two years, in accordance with our UK Recruitment Privacy Notice / EU Recruitment Privacy Notice, to evaluate your application and meet our legal and reporting obligations. In line with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), you have the right to request access to, rectification, or erasure (subject to legal limitations) of your personal data. For more information, please contact us at privacy@baringa.com

For the USA

Your personal data may be retained by Baringa for up to two years, as outlined in our Recruitment Privacy Notice (AMER & APAC), to support the recruitment process and internal reporting requirements. Where applicable, and in accordance with relevant federal and state laws, you may have the right to request access to or correction of your personal information. For further details, please contact privacy@baringa.com

For Australia & Singapore

Your personal data will be retained by Baringa for up to two years, in accordance with our Recruitment Privacy Notice (AMER & APAC), to assess your application and meet applicable reporting and legal obligations. In line with the Australian Privacy Act and Singapore’s Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA), you may have rights to access, correct, or request limited deletion of your personal data. For more information, please contact us at privacy@baringa.com

rows.title: Data Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
About Independent Media

Independent Media comprises The Independent, Standard Digital, Bulletin, BuzzFeed UK, HuffPost UK, Tasty UK, Seasoned, IndyBest and indy100.

Harnessing market-leading innovation and excellence across its portfolio of pioneering brands, Independent Media has unrivalled scale, integrity and authority via its sites, apps, video, audio, experiential, newsletters and social media.

While each Independent Media brand speaks in an authentic, unique voice to a loyal and distinct audience, they stand together in their commitment to positivity, inclusivity, and quality journalism and content.

Independent Media’s network reaches 650 million users each month, with 1.1 billion content views across its brands and platforms, including web, apps, social media, podcasts, email, YouTube, syndication partners and print.

The role and the team

As a Data Analyst, you will support the Digital Analytics team in providing reporting, analysis and insight across Independent Media, with a particular focus on understanding how our journalism and content performs across our digital platforms and syndication partners.

Working closely with analysts and stakeholders across Editorial, Audience, Product, Commercial Licensing & Syndication and Marketing teams, you will help produce regular performance reporting, maintain dashboards and respond to day-to-day analytical requests.

This would suit someone with some experience working with digital or audience data who is looking to develop their career in analytics within a fast-paced news and publishing environment.

You will be responsible for:

Compile regular editorial and management reports using key audience and content data sources.Support the Licensing & Syndication team with reporting and analysis to understand how our content performs across third-party and off-platform partners.Support analysis of website traffic, audience engagement, search, social media and video performance.Work with the Customer Analytics and Marketing teams to track and analyse marketing activity, helping to understand how campaigns drive users through the registration and subscription funnels and increase audience frequency and engagement.Use GA4 and other analytics platforms to investigate changes and trends in audience behaviour.Help maintain BI dashboards and recurring reports used by stakeholders across the business.Monitor performance and highlight significant or unusual changes that may require further investigation.Support the team with ad hoc analytical requests, ensuring outputs are accurate and delivered within agreed deadlines.Work with editorial and audience teams to help them understand how their content is performing.Use SEO and search performance tools to understand how content performs through search e.g. Google Search ConsoleAnalyse social media performance using relevant platform metrics and analytics tools e.g. SupermetricsHelp ensure reporting definitions and methodologies are applied consistently.Carry out appropriate quality assurance and sense-checking before data or analysis is shared.Develop a working knowledge of the databases, analytics platforms and reporting tools used across the business.Handle data responsibly and securely, in accordance with GDPR, the Data Protection Act and the Company’s Code of Conduct.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

We champion diversity in our teams and in our reporting. As a growing and global brand, we must have a workforce that’s more representative of our readers, viewers, clients and partners, and a workplace that creates a sense of belonging for everyoneWe are committed to hiring and developing a diverse workforce regardless of background, and we support our people to thrive in their careers here.

The Independent is an equal opportunities employer, if you require any reasonable adjustments to complete your application, please do not hesitate to advise us accordingly.

About You

You are curious, analytical and have a strong attention to detail. You enjoy solving problems and investigating why something has happened rather than simply reporting the numbers.

You have an interest in news, digital publishing and how audiences discover and engage with content online. You will have some previous experience in an analytics, insights, digital marketing or similar role and be keen to develop your skills further.

You should be comfortable working with data and able to communicate your findings clearly to colleagues with different levels of data knowledge.

Essential Skills And Experience

Degree level, ideally in a numerate, analytical or relevant subject.Around 1-2 years’ experience in an analytics, insights, digital marketing or similar data-focused role.Excellent attention to detail and a commitment to producing accurate, reliable work.Strong problem-solving skills and a curious approach to data, with an interest in understanding the reasons behind changes in performance.Experience using GA4 or another digital analytics platform, such as Adobe Analytics.Good working knowledge of Excel or Google Sheets.An interest in news, digital publishing and audience behaviour.An ability to interpret data and communicate findings clearly to non-technical colleagues.Good organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple requests and deadlines.Good written and verbal communication skills.A collaborative approach and willingness to learn new tools and techniques.

Desirable Skills And Experience

Experience analysing social media metrics across platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, TikTok or YouTube.Experience working with BI or visualisation tools such as Domo, Looker, Tableau or Power BI.Some knowledge of SQL or an interest in developing SQL skills.Experience working with content, audience or editorial data.Previous experience within digital publishing, media or a newsroom environment.Familiarity with tools such as Chartbeat or other real-time audience analytics platforms.An understanding of how SEO, social media and other referral channels contribute to digital audience growth.Key responsibilities and accountabilities

Our values – you will deliver across all our values

Inclusive: We champion diversity in our teams and in our reporting. Working as a team, we put transparency and effective communication at the heart of everything we do.

Innovative: From the very beginning, The Independent has been breaking the mould. We take risks and are always looking to try new ideas in pursuit of excellence.

Independent: Nobody tells us what to think; we make up our own minds and aren’t afraid to do things differently. Like our readers, we value honesty and integrity above outside influences.

rows.descriptionText:
Job Description

To solve complex challenges, you need to challenge the status-quo

At GHD Advisory we are invested in creating sustainable commercial outcomes with clients driving change in water, energy and urbanization.

Join a team committed to solving complex challenges across the value chain, from capital deployment to asset management, enabling resilience, growth and sustainability.

Together, we’ll help create a future for generations to come.

Who are we looking for?

We are recruiting for our September 2027 Graduate Data Consultant intake and are looking for ambitious students and recent graduates eager to develop technical and consulting skills while working on meaningful client projects. As part of GHD's global Advisory business, our Data & Insights team works across infrastructure, transport, energy, water and government to help clients make better decisions.  Support the analysis of complex datasets to help clients understand performance, demand and operational challenges.  Contribute to the development of analytical models and decision-support tools.  A degree in a relevant discipline such as Data Science, Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Geography, Engineering, Physics or a related field.  Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to approach complex challenges in a structured way.  An interest in using data and technology to support decision-making and solve real-world problems.  The ability to communicate ideas clearly, both verbally and in writing.  Curiosity, initiative and a willingness to learn new skills and technologies.  A collaborative approach and an ability to work effectively with people from different backgrounds and disciplines.  Attention to detail and a commitment to delivering high-quality work.  An interest in developing both technical expertise and consulting skills.  An enthusiasm for working with clients and understanding the challenges they face.

rows.title: Senior Value Analyst HE
rows.descriptionText:
Agency

Adelphi

Job Function

Data and Analytics

Job Subfunction

Data Engineering

Job Description

Company: Adelphi Values Limited, part of Adelphi Group (an Omnicom Healthcare Company)

What We’re Looking For

This position would suit an enthusiastic, dynamic individual looking to use their scientific and HE technical hands-on background within a fast-paced environment offering the opportunity to gain a broader and global commercial insight and application. The role presents an opportunity for career development in a fun, hardworking team in a dynamic, growing consultancy. We are looking for an ambitious Senior Value Analyst with a passion for understanding and communicating the science of healthcare value. You must hold a health economics postgraduate qualification and 1-2 years of relevant work experience in a consultancy, HTA organisation, academia or industry. In addition to excellent analytical skills, you will be able to demonstrate research skills, a creative, solution-driven mind-set, excellent interpretative and writing skills, and an ability to communicate scientific material clearly in both written and oral form. Hands on experience of building economic models (cost-effectiveness and budget impact) and in interpreting results from economic models is also necessary, and experience in undertaking systematic reviews and meta-analysis would be highly desirable. Fluency in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint, organisation skills, self-motivation and very close attention to detail are essential, along with a team work ethos and an appetite for working in a fast-paced environment (and having fun)!

How You Fit In

The role involves contributing to delivering health economics solutions to our international clients by investigation, evaluation and problem solving. You will also research and investigate the multiple perspectives of patient, healthcare professionals, payers and policy makers. With each new client, from small biotech start-ups to the world’s leading pharmaceutical companies, you will be constantly learning about new medicines, disease areas, drug approval processes and markets. We promise you’ll never be bored! We are committed to your development, and you will receive one-to-one and group training on various technical aspects along with opportunities for progression.

What a career at Adelphi Values PROVE can offer you

Opportunities at Adelphi Values PROVE provide the perfect opportunity to develop your career in the healthcare industry consultancy with a focus on HEOR and Market Access. You’ll be working in a supportive team where your contribution will be valued and your development and professional growth is seen as a priority. With this in mind, training is available at every stage of your career.

We enjoy spending time together as a team, running regular socials. Recent activities have included quiz evenings, local team walks, Quarterly meetings and regular get togethers. Giving back has always been important to our team, each year we support one charity, as well as having fundraising activities across our offices.

As well as a supportive, fun and collaborative team you’ll have access to the following benefits:

 Competitive compensation package Private Healthcare (Including couples and family options) Life insurance Income protection insurance Gym Membership Further training and development

Who We Are

Adelphi Values PROVE is a leading healthcare value consultancy that works with a range of healthcare product and service providers, aiding development and commercialisation. We are passionate people working as integrated global teams, growing a respected healthcare value consultancy business that is committed to personal development and rewarding high performance. We are as proud of our culture and our approach to people and their working environment, as we are of our reputation and the things that make us unique.

Our purpose is to improve patients’ lives by informing healthcare decisions. To do this we help our clients bring healthcare products and services to the market successfully by investigating, developing and communicating scientific evidence that defines value and informs decisions.

Adelphi Values PROVE™ is part of the Adelphi Group. Adelphi’s offer spans the lifecycle of pharmaceutical development, with comprehensive services in Strategic Product Development Consultancy, Health Economics and Outcomes Research, Real World Disease Understanding, Marketing Research, Medical Communications and Post-meeting Brand Support Services. Adelphi has a global network of offices across US, Europe and Asia and over 800 staff worldwide.

To all applicants: in line with legislation, this position is only open to candidates who have indefinite eligibility to work in the UK. Please provide relevant details of your eligibility within your application.

Omnicom’s policy requires employees to work in the office for a minimum of three days a week, unless additional in-office days are directed by their agency or manager. Our objective is to increase this requirement over time, and many of our agencies as well as Omnicom’s corporate group already require five days of in-office attendance.

Omnicom is committed to hiring and developing exceptional talent. We agree that talent is uniquely distributed, and we’re focused on developing inclusive teams that can bring the best solutions to everything we do. We strongly believe that celebrating what makes us different makes us better together. Join us—we look forward to getting to know you. We will process your personal data in accordance with our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

Link to Recruitment Privacy Notice: https://www.omc.com/privacy-notice/

rows.title: Graduate, Transactional Business Planning & Insights
rows.descriptionText:
Please note that this role is based in the United Kingdom. To enable us to meet the statutory and regulatory obligations of the United Kingdom immigration system, you must have the appropriate immigration permission needed to work and reside in the United Kingdom for the duration of the employment.

Job Description

The EMEA Transactional Business Planning & Insights Graduate plays an important role in supporting data-driven decision-making across Sony Pictures' International Home Entertainment business. Working alongside the Senior Managers, the Analyst provides analytical support through the preparation of reports, dashboards, forecasting models and commercial insights that enable informed business decisions across EMEA.

This role is ideally suited to an inquisitive and technically capable analyst who enjoys working with large datasets, identifying trends and solving business problems through data. The successful candidate will help maintain the reporting and analytical infrastructure that supports Business Planning & Insights while continually looking for opportunities to improve reporting, automate processes and uncover new commercial insights.

Reporting to the Senior Manager, EMEA Transactional Business Planning & Insights, the Analyst will work closely with Commercial, Finance, Marketing, Research and Global colleagues to ensure accurate, timely and insightful analysis that supports forecasting, planning and retailer engagement.

Reporting & Analytics

Produce regular and ad-hoc reports that support Commercial, Finance and Business Planning teams across EMEA.Build and maintain dashboards using Tableau, Power BI or similar reporting tools to provide clear and actionable business insights.Analyse large datasets to identify trends, opportunities, anomalies and emerging business issues.Develop reporting solutions that improve visibility of business performance and support data-driven decision-making.Ensure reporting outputs are accurate, timely and presented in a clear and meaningful way.

Data Management & Business Intelligence

Maintain and validate datasets used across Business Planning & Insights activities, ensuring high levels of accuracy and consistency.Support the management of reporting databases and analytical models across multiple business areas.Perform regular data quality checks and investigate anomalies where identified.Assist in integrating multiple internal and external data sources to create meaningful commercial insights.Contribute to maintaining a single source of truth for Business Planning & Insights reporting.

Forecasting & Commercial Support

Support the preparation and maintenance of forecasting models for New Release and Catalogue planning.Produce financial reports and variance analysis to support business planning activities.Assist with the preparation of analytical material for retailer meetings, Joint Business Planning sessions and commercial reviews.Provide analytical support for pricing, promotions and title performance evaluations.Support budget and forecasting submissions through accurate data preparation and model maintenance.

Process Improvement & Automation

Proactively identify opportunities to improve reporting processes through automation and simplification.Develop more efficient reporting solutions using Excel, Tableau, SQL, Power BI or other analytical tools.Explore emerging technologies, including AI-assisted analytical tools, that could improve efficiency and insight generation.Support continuous improvement initiatives across reporting, forecasting and analytical processes.

Collaboration & Global Alignment

Build effective relationships across Commercial, Finance, Marketing, Research and Global teams.Support Senior Managers by preparing analysis and presentations for business reviews and customer meetings.Share insights and analytical findings clearly with colleagues across the business.Contribute to a collaborative culture focused on continuous improvement and data-driven decision-making.

Qualifications

Knowledge

Around 1-3 years' experience in an analytical, reporting, business intelligence or commercial analysis role.Experience working with large datasets and producing meaningful business insights.Exposure to business reporting, dashboards or performance analysis within a commercial environment.Solid grounding in financial planning, forecasting, and performance analytics.Experience in digital distribution, home entertainment, or global media strategy is desired but not essential.Experience working across multiple international territories, with exposure to EMEA markets would be beneficial.

Skills

Highly proficient in Excel and PowerPoint, with the ability to translate data into actionable insights.Experience using Tableau, Power BI or similar Business Intelligence tools.Working knowledge of SQL for querying and manipulating data.Experience using reporting databases and data visualisation tools.Experience with Python, Alteryx or AI-enabled analytical tools would be advantageous but not essential.Excellent written and verbal communication, capable of presenting findings to senior stakeholders with clarity and impact.

Core Competencies

Analytical ThinkingCuriosityProblem SolvingLearning AgilityAttention to DetailCommunicationCollaboration

How We Take Care Of You

Competitive salary, with annual bonus eligibility.A choice of comprehensive health plan options that fit your lifestyle, including private medical insurance.Rest and recharge during a week off during the winter holidays, in addition to the 25 days of paid annual leave.Participate in extensive learning & development opportunities at all levels, including curated instructor-led classes and high-impact online resources.Build your community by joining our Employee Business Resource Groups.Access to an employee online store filled with a variety of discounted Sony products.Watch the newest movies and TV shows at our exclusive employee screenings at work.Entitlement to apply for an interest-free season ticket loan.Automatic enrolment in the Company’s Pension Plan.Free counselling and advisory service.Automatic enrolment in the Company’s Life Insurance and Group Income Protection Plans, subject to any applicable service requirements.The opportunity to attend various social events in our state-of-the-art offices in Paddington.Range of other optional discounted benefits that are reviewed regularly (e.g., gym memberships, travel insurance, activity passes, car leasing, experience days and many more!).

rows.title: Systems Data Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Overview

Home. There's no place like it.

And there's no feeling like helping people create the joy of feeling truly at home. At Dunelm, that's what we do. We're the UK's number one choice for homewares because we make home life lovelier for our customers. And we've crafted a workplace that feels just as welcoming, where you can bring your ideas, be yourself, and feel right at home.

Work your way, together

We're a hybrid business, which means you'll have flexibility alongside time together with your team. In this role, you can expect 2 days per week in our Leicester or London office, helping you stay connected, collaborate and do your best work for our customers.

The Systems Data Analyst plays a critical role in ensuring that data from Dunelm’s core systems is accurately understood, clearly defined and ready for engineering delivery. The role acts as the bridge between source systems and data engineering teams, providing detailed system and data analysis that underpins high-quality data products.

Working closely with Data Product Managers, Data Management, Data Engineers and business stakeholders, the Systems Data Analyst translates business questions into precise, system-level data requirements. This includes analysing source systems, defining data structures, producing data models and mappings, and ensuring requirements are development-ready before build begins.

What you'll be doing

Understand the data lifecycle and originating business process flows architecting as-is and to be flows where requiredAnalyse source systems and integrations to understand data structures, relationships and behavioursPerform end-to-end data flow analysis into the enterprise data platformIdentify data quality issues, ambiguities and risks in source dataRequirements refinement and definitionUtilise requirements definition to inform scope andrequired data management activities.Translate business needs into clear, system-level data requirementsEnsure data requirements meet Definition of Ready standardsData modelling and documentationStructured and logical explanations of process flows, intersection with business process and system/data outputs & outcomes in appropriate mediums (presentations, PRD's etc)Produce conceptual, logical and physical data modelsDefine and maintain source-to-target data mappings

What we'll look for in you

Essential Skills And Experience

Strong analytical and system analysis skillsExperience producing data models and data requirements, including conceptual, logical and physicalStrong SQL skills for data validationExposure to PythonExperience with enterprise data platformsClear written and verbal communicationAbility to produce structured, reusable documentationAn inquisitive and curious mindsetCollaborative and T-shaped; willing to contribute where required to get the job done

Nice To Haves

Exposure to ETL / ELT pipelinesRetail systems experience (ERP, POS, Supply Chain, Digital)Experience working in Agile delivery environmentsInterest in responsible AI and model governance

Key qualities, behaviours and values

Making it happen – proactively identify risks and validate assumptionsActing like an owner – taking responsibility for the reliability and quality of the services you supportKeep listening and learning – curious, open to feedback and committed to continuous improvementStronger together – collaborative and inclusive when working across disciplines

rows.title: Insight Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Weekly office requirement: Minimum 1 day per week - Wednesdays

Employment type: Permanent

Seniority level: Entry

Language: All stages of the recruitment process will be conducted in English

At GWI we’re always looking for extraordinary people who thrive on making an extraordinary impact. Right now we’re looking for an Insight Analyst to play a key role in our Insight Services team in London. If that’s you, and making a difference gets you out of bed in the morning, keep reading. It could be the start of something, well, extraordinary.

Sounds great, what will I be doing? 🤔

As an Insight Analyst, you'll be passionate about uncovering data-driven stories that shape how our Agency clients understand their audiences. In this role, you’ll turn GWI’s rich datasets into compelling insights, reports, and presentations that reveal the unexpected and make our clients’ strategies sharper.

A few things you'll be responsible for:

👉 Support and lead projects for our agency clients - turning complex data into clear, actionable narratives through high-quality deliverables decks, reports and one-pagers

👉 Analyze GWI datasets to surface trends and patterns that align with client objectives

👉 Own the quality of your outputs - ensuring they're accurate, timely, and follow department best practice

👉 Keeping up with the latest news and developments impacting the industry and our clients

👉 Contributing to non-client specific assets that drive awareness and engagement with potential clients

👉 Partner closely with our Revenue team on incoming projects

👉 Present insights confidently to clients and internal teams when required

It's also fun; shaking things up is what working for GWI is all about. You'll need to be flexible, comfortable with continuous change, and working in a high-tempo environment.

What do I need to bring with me? 🧳

You'll need to be able to demonstrate the core skills this role requires. You don't have to tick all the boxes right away; the important thing is that you're willing to learn. Here's what the team will be looking for in you:

👉 Proven experience as a researcher or analyst, ideally in market research

👉 A talent for data storytelling - translating numbers into narratives

👉 Exceptional attention to detail and a flair for writing clear, engaging content

👉 Experience managing client-facing projects and delivering to tight deadlines

👉 Strong skills in Microsoft Office, especially Excel and PowerPoint; Google Slides experience is a plus

👉 Excellent organization, time management, and collaboration skills

👉 Experience with, or willingness to adopt, AI-powered solutions

Equally important is attitude. We want people who think big (to make an impact), ask why (to find a better way), and show respect (to everyone, at every level, all the time). Those are our values, and they're a big part of what we're looking for in you.

Why Join Us


Be part of a close-knit global team which encourages innovation, thinking big and close collaboration.Contribute to diverse projects that span multiple sectors and audiences.Enjoy a fast-growth environment with opportunities to learn, grow and make a tangible impact. Enjoy a package built around flexibility: hybrid working, flexitime, and early Friday finishes in summer


What We Offer 🧘

At GWI, you’ll find meaningful work, visible impact, and a culture that empowers you to do your best. Our package includes:


Time to recharge – 25 days’ annual leave, plus office closures over the holidays.Health & wellbeing – Health cash plan, enhanced family benefits, carer days, and mental health support.Financial benefits – Competitive salary, 4% pension matching, and recognition programs that celebrate success.Flexibility & balance – Flexitime, early Friday finishes, hybrid and remote options, plus a “work from home” budget.Career growth – Accredited learning, leadership development, and global career mobility.Community & impact – DE&I initiatives, volunteering opportunities, donation matching, and payroll giving.


Put all that together and GWI is the friendliest, most fulfilling place any of us has ever worked.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion 🫶

Diversity is fundamental to who we are—as a data company and as a workplace. Our data reflects global realities, and so must our teams. We strive to build a workforce as diverse and inclusive as the insights we deliver.

As a Disability Confident employer, we welcome applications from disabled candidates and are committed to making adjustments throughout the hiring process—whether that's extra time, materials in advance or a different format, breaks, an adjusted interview format, assistive tools, or flexible scheduling. We're happy to discuss whatever would work best for you.

We actively encourage applications from underrepresented and marginalised communities.

At GWI, you'll find a place to contribute meaningfully, grow professionally, and belong fully.

rows.title: Insights Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
About Elevate

Elevate is a full-service consulting firm that inspires high-performing organizations to find their limits and push past them. With expertise in brand consulting, sales strategy, data-driven insights, and talent optimization, Elevate gives its clients a competitive edge in the fight for people’s precious time and attention. Established in 2018, Elevate set out to help sports teams and leagues spark innovation and drive performance. In the years since, the world of sports has transformed, today standing at the convergence of media, entertainment, and consumer brands, with Elevate supporting some of the world’s most ambitious businesses across these sectors. Elevate’s proprietary technology, data sources, and software products combined with our thoughtful insights, and people-centric approach give clients a 360-degree view of their customers, underpinning intelligent decision-making on marketing spend, growth strategy, and more.

Our team of 700+ employees spans the globe with in 20 locations worldwide. We value recruiting diverse individuals to our team to bring new perspectives to our company and look forward to learning more about you in the recruitment process. To learn more and see what we’ve been up to, follow Elevate on X, LinkedIn, and Instagram.

Overview

Elevate operates as a fully integrated partner for its clients, adding insight, expertise, and in-market marquee asset sales activity to accelerate and enhance revenue in collaboration with the client’s leadership, partnership teams and wider stakeholder landscape (e.g. marketing and brand, hospitality, technology, community, venue operations, etc.)

Elevate is seeking a passionate and talented individual to join our Strategy and Insights team within the International Partnerships department. Based in London, the ideal candidate will have a deep interest in sports and a proven ability to research and analyse businesses across various industries. We value curiosity and seek someone who can methodically channel their efforts to deliver actionable insights that drive success across sponsorship sales projects. The role requires creativity in aligning brands with sports properties and the ability to communicate ideas effectively through both written and verbal formats. The candidate will also play a key role in sourcing, managing, and leveraging data to build value for rights holders and venues. A flair for crafting innovative materials and creating compelling sales narratives to support our objectives is essential

Key Deliverables

Conduct detailed research on companies, including spend analysis, target geographies, marketing budgets, and previous sponsorship activities, as well as broader industry trends to identify opportunities and inform strategy.Create and maintain organised data sets and dashboards in Excel to house research findings, ensuring accessibility and usability for the broader team.Develop creative brand alignment concepts in collaboration with the Partnerships team, leveraging research to match brands with sports properties effectively.Provide ongoing support for sales conversations by sourcing relevant information, crafting tailored materials, and contributing insights to enhance client engagement.Manage reporting processes, ensuring accurate and timely updates for both internal stakeholders and clients, and oversee the effective use of the CRM system to track progress and outcomes.Collaborate with internal teams to produce impactful sales narratives and presentations, translating research and insights into compelling client-facing materials.Support the preparation and execution of sales pitches, client meetings, and brand negotiations by articulating insights and presenting data confidently in both written and verbal formats.Support with managing relationships with data providers, including briefing on requirements, monitoring data delivery, and maintaining effective partnerships.

PERSON SPECIFICATION

Demonstrates a genuine passion for sports and a strong interest in understanding its intersection with business and sponsorships.Combines analytical and creative thinking to uncover insights, identify opportunities, and translate them into actionable strategies.Enjoys conducting thorough research, demonstrating curiosity and the ability to investigate topics on a deeper level.Proficient in Microsoft Excel, with the ability to organise and analyse data effectively, as well as experience in creating professional and visually engaging presentation slides.Experience using CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce) is highly desirable, with the capability to manage and utilise client and sales data efficiently.Possesses excellent interpersonal and communication skills, enabling clear articulation of ideas and confident collaboration with team members, clients, and stakeholders.A strong team player who is adaptable and proactive in providing support and contributing to shared goals.Able to balance multiple priorities and meet deadlines under pressure while maintaining a high standard of work.Goal-oriented with a results-driven mindset and a commitment to delivering exceptional outcomes.Ability to work in the UK

Benefits Overview

Insurance (Company‑Paid)

Elevate provides the following benefits, effective from your first day of employment:

Medical - Elevate covers 100% of your premium. Dependants can be added at your own cost via payroll deductionsDental and Optician ReimbursementTravel Insurance - Elevate covers 100% of your premium. Dependants may be added at your costLife Assurance - Fully employer‑paid, covering 4× your basic annual salary up to a free cover limit of £800,000Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) - Fully employer‑funded

Time Off

33 days annual leave, inclusive of the 8 UK bank holidaysUp to 10 days paid sick leave within a rolling 12‑month period

Pension

4% employer contribution 5% employee contribution (based on full salary via salary sacrifice)

This position is open to all qualified candidates. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability in connection with the application process, you may contact us at HR@oneelevate.com

We are proud to be an equal opportunity/veterans/disabled/ LGBT employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All employment is decided based on qualifications, merit, and business need, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.
